meta.scope: Indonesia Batch 12 — Energy mix & power generation, oil & natural gas production, religious composition statistics, and related supporting nodes. Chosen as high-value remaining uniqueness: coal-dominated power system, declining oil / substantial gas, and the world’s largest Muslim-majority population with official multi-religion statistics.

candidates.title: Electricity generation by source / power-plant type
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources related
candidates.description: Statistics on electricity production by generation type. Coal-fired (PLTU) remains dominant; gas, hydro, geothermal and other sources make up the balance. Total generation has been rising with demand.
candidates.notes: Core power-mix node. Coal dominance is a central structural feature of the Indonesian energy system.

candidates.title: Energy Balance of Indonesia (detailed production–consumption)
candidates.description: Official energy balance covering production through final consumption for oil, gas, coal and renewables. Extends the earlier Energy Balances node with fuller multi-year detail.
referenced_by: Coal, oil and gas production series

candidates.title: Crude oil and condensate production statistics
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
candidates.description: Long-run series of petroleum and condensate production. Shows the long-term decline from earlier peak levels; Indonesia is no longer a net oil exporter in the classic sense.
candidates.notes: Declining-oil production node — important contrast with the still-large coal and gas roles.

candidates.title: Natural gas production statistics
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
candidates.description: Natural gas production series (MMscf). Gas remains a significant domestic and export energy commodity and feeds both power generation and industrial use / LNG.
candidates.notes: Gas-side counterpart to the oil and coal nodes.

candidates.title: Religious composition statistics (Islam, Christianity, Hinduism, Buddhism, etc.)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs (Dukcapil) / Population Census / BPS-related
candidates.description: Official population statistics by religion. Islam constitutes the large majority (~87 %); Protestant, Catholic, Hindu, Buddhist, Confucian and other recognised categories make up the remainder. Continuously cited in social, cultural and political analysis.
referenced_by: Regional cultural and political analysis (e.g. Bali Hindu concentration)
candidates.notes: Foundational social-identity node. Indonesia is the world’s largest Muslim-majority country; the official multi-religion statistics also capture significant Christian, Hindu and other communities.

candidates.title: Geographic distribution of religious communities
candidates.publisher: Derived from census and civil-registration data
candidates.description: Spatial patterning of religious affiliation — Muslim majority almost everywhere, with notable Hindu concentration in Bali, Christian majorities or large minorities in parts of eastern Indonesia (North Sulawesi, Papua, Maluku, NTT, etc.), and other local patterns.
referenced_by: Provincial and Bali–Nusa Tenggara / Papua / Sulawesi nodes
candidates.notes: Spatial densification of the religion cluster; links identity to the archipelagic geography already mapped.

candidates.title: Geothermal power and renewable generation statistics
candidates.publisher: BPS / Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources related
candidates.description: Statistics on geothermal (PLTP) and other renewable generation. Indonesia has one of the world’s largest geothermal resource bases; actual generation remains a smaller but stable share of the mix.
referenced_by: Energy Balances and NDC / energy-transition documents
candidates.notes: Renewable-side densification of the energy cluster; geothermal is a distinctive Indonesian asset.

candidates.title: Energy-transition and renewable-policy framing
candidates.publisher: Government of Indonesia / MEMR / related planning documents
candidates.description: Recurring policy framing around energy transition, renewable targets and the tension with continued coal dominance in the power sector. Continuously cited alongside NDC and long-term planning documents.
referenced_by: Electricity mix, coal and GHG nodes
candidates.notes: Policy-frame node for the energy-transition debate.

candidates.title: Indonesia energy-mix–oil-gas–religion densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS, MEMR, Dukcapil and related sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding electricity generation by source, detailed energy balances, oil and gas production, geothermal/renewables, energy-transition framing, religious composition and religious geography into a coherent energy-and-identity layer.
referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier coal, energy-balance, GHG, Islamic-finance and provincial series
